Analytic particle templates based on the stationary-phase approximation perform reasonably well for the \((\ell,m)=(2,2)\) multipole, but exhibit substantial limitations for the \((4,4)\). Although the filter is all-pass, it substantially affects the modeling results. Our analytic calculations on a Schwarzschild background further show that vacuum perturbations with Gaussian initial data can also exhibit direct-wave-like waveforms after filtering, with their morphology depending on the location of the initial data relative to the light ring.

papers.title: Post-adiabatic effective-one-body waveforms for coalescing compact binaries
papers.abstract: I apply and extend the formalism of osculating orbits of Damour et al. (2004) and Lynch et al. (2026) to eccentric effective one body (EOB) models, in order to obtain an efficient yet accurate description of the inspiral-to-plunge dynamics of tidal, spinning compact binaries, including precessing ones by twisting the otherwise planar motion. The method is recast in terms of equinoctial orbital elements, to circumvent singularities associated with the zero-eccentricity limit. While the formalism is general and can be applied to any EOB model, I focus here on the TEOBResumS-Dalí family and demonstrate how this technique speeds up waveform generation without significantly compromising the accuracy of the model. papers.title: Inaccessibility of the Cosmological Singularity to Quantum Probes
papers.abstract: We propose an operational resolution of the FLRW big bang singularity using quantum probes satisfying a curvature coupled Klein-Gordon equation. The classical big bang surface is therefore inaccessible to this class of quantum probes in finite effective proper time, while the underlying FLRW spacetime remains singular.

papers.title: Optimal galaxy magnification: generalized fundamental-plane residuals and number counts are all you need
papers.abstract: Weak-lensing magnification complements cosmic shear through its effects on galaxy fluxes, sizes, and number counts. We derive the optimal magnification statistics from galaxy properties and show that the optimal measurement can be decomposed into an optimal mean statistic and total number counts. The optimal mean statistic can be constructed from the residual distribution of a generalized fundamental plane (GFP), $F(i,\boldsymbol{X})$, which predicts galaxy size or, equivalently, flux from surface brightness $i$ and additional lensing-invariant properties $\boldsymbol{X}$. The function $F$ can take any form that reduces the intrinsic scatter and thereby improves magnification precision. For a Gaussian residual distribution, the optimal mean statistic reduces to the inverse-variance-weighted residual, or simply the residual for constant scatter. Together with total number counts, this statistic captures all the magnification Fisher information under Poisson statistics, achieving the same precision as a full-likelihood analysis. This provides a simple and physically intuitive optimal compression of the full magnification likelihood, avoiding the need to model the potentially high-dimensional galaxy-property distribution, particularly when additional observables are incorporated to reduce the GFP scatter. Our results demonstrate that GFP residuals and number counts provide an optimal combination for weak-lensing magnification measurements in galaxy surveys.

papers.title: Entanglement entropy of near-extremal black hole
papers.abstract: We study how the entanglement entropy of the Hawking radiation derived using island recipe for the Reissner-Nordström black hole behaves as the black hole mass decreases. A general answer to the question essentially depends not only on the character of decreasing of the mass but also on decreasing of the charge. We assume the specific relationship between the charge and mass $Q^2=GM^2[1-\left(\frac{M}{\mu}\right)^{2\nu} ]$, which we call the constraint equation. We discuss whether it is possible to have a constraint so that the entanglement entropy does not have an explosion at the end of evaporation, as happens in the case of thermodynamic entropy and the entanglement entropy for the Schwarzschild black hole. We show that for some special scaling parameters, the entanglement entropy of radiation does not explode as long as the mass of the evaporating black hole exceeds the Planck mass.

papers.title: Cosmological Constant and Maximum of Entropy for de Sitter Space
papers.abstract: There are at least two cosmological constants calling for explanation. The first one describes the quasi-de Sitter inflation in the early universe, and the second describes the current acceleration of the universe associated with dark energy. An approach to the computation of the inflationary cosmological constant in the early universe is proposed. The tunneling and no-boundary proposals suggest that the ground state of the early universe is the de Sitter space. In this paper it is argued that the radius of the de Sitter space, i.e. the cosmological constant, can be computed using the principle of maximum entropy. The universe emerges from ``nothing" that corresponds to a minimum of entropy. The entropy reaches its maximal value for the 4-dimensional de Sitter space with the inflationary cosmological constant $\Lambda=3\pi\,\exp\{-\psi(3/2)\}$, where $\psi$ is the digamma function, $\Lambda\approx 9.087$ in Planck units.

papers.title: Information Problem in Black Holes and Cosmology and Ghosts in Quadratic Gravity
papers.abstract: Black hole information problem is the question about unitarity of the evolution operator during the collapse and evaporation of the black hole. One can ask the same question about unitarity of quantum and inflationary cosmology. In this paper we argue that in both cases, for black holes and for cosmology, the answer is negative and we face non-unitarity. Such a question can not be addressed by using the fixed classical gravitational background since one has to take into account the backreaction. To his end one uses the semi-classical gravity, which includes the expectation value of the energy - momentum tensor operator of the matter fields. One has to renormalize the energy-momentum tensor and one gets an effective action which contains quadratic terms in scalar curvature and Ricci tensor. Such quadratic gravity contains ghosts which in fact lead to violation of unitarity in black holes and cosmology. We discuss the question whether black holes will emit ghosts. One can try to restrict ourselves to the $f(R)$ gravity that seems is a good approximation to the semi-classical gravity and widely used in cosmology. The black hole entropy in $f(R)$ gravity is different from the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and from entanglement island entropy. The black hole entropy in $R+R^2$ gravity goes to a constant during the evaporation process. This can be interpreted as another indication to the possible non-unitarity in black holes and cosmology

papers.title: Triaxiality of the Milky Way dark matter halo and the microlensing optical depth towards the Large Magellanic Cloud
papers.abstract: The microlensing optical depth towards the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), $\tau_{\rm LMC}$, bounds the compact-object fraction of the Galactic dark matter halo, but is almost always evaluated for a spherical halo. We compute it for triaxial haloes and show that the shape dependence is carried entirely by the projection of the line of sight onto the halo principal axes: for a scale-free halo $\rho\propto R^{-\alpha}$ at fixed local density it factorises exactly as $\tau/\tau_{\rm sph}=S_\odot^{\alpha}\langle S^{-\alpha}\rangle_w$, with $S(\Omega)$ the ellipsoidal shape function. The LMC lies only $0\fdg78$ from perpendicular to the Sun-Galactic Centre line, making it a near-optimal probe of in-plane elongation and a poor probe of vertical flattening. For the halo shapes favoured by \textit{Gaia} we find $\tau_{\rm LMC}/\tau_{\rm sph}=0.95$--$1.15$ at fixed local density, $1.57$ for the Law-Majewski logarithmic potential, and $0.67$--$1.54$ when the major-axis azimuth is left free. For the Einasto halo required by the declining \textit{Gaia} DR3 rotation curve, truncation near $25\kpc$ is offset by the larger local density it implies and $\tau$ falls by only $7$--$15$ per cent; but the median lens distance moves inwards from $13.4$ to $8.5\kpc$, where the logarithmic slope is steep and rising, amplifying the shape sensitivity: the \textit{Gaia} RR~Lyrae enhancement grows from $15$ to $23$ per cent and the orientation-free range widens to $0.62$--$1.62$. The systematic on the inferred MACHO or primordial-black-hole fraction is two-sided, of order $\pm15$ per cent for the measured shapes and a factor $2.6$ under full orientation freedom, exceeding the statistical errors of the EROS-2 and OGLE bounds.

papers.title: The variance of the CMB temperature gradient: a dependence on the spatial orientation and anisotropy of a multiply connected Universe
papers.abstract: In the present work we develop a model--independent method to reveal the underlying patterns of anisotropy and geometry in CMB temperature maps. This method, based on the rho-statistics and a process of mask--sweeping, unveils faint but persistent geometrical and periodic structures characterising the anisotropy of the CMB in a universe with 3-torus topology. We assess that the patterns detected over large ensembles of toroidal maps match geometrically to the layouts of expected circles-in-the-sky. The mask--sweeping method explores the whole CMB over 768 mask orientations. Thus we are able to re-verify the linear relation between L the size of the cubic torus and rho the standard deviation of the normalised variance of the CMB temperature gradient. This confers a finite size s of approximately 3 Hubble lengths to our Universe with toroidal topology. Furthermore, it is shown that the violation of statistical isotropy is so faint that this has almost no influence on the linear relation between rho and L. A topology like the cubic toroidal one imposes to our Universe periodic conditions (that can be seen as periodic boundary conditions) which constrain the global degree of inhomogeneity and a zero average curvature. We demonstrate here that rho is not only a statistical signature of the spatial finiteness and size of our Universe (may its topology be simply or multiply connected) but also outlines the patterns of anisotropy of the CMB with the help of the mask--sweeping process.

papers.title: Testing the statistical compatibility of data sets with a common prior
papers.abstract: The Parameter Goodness-of-fit (PG) test [hep-ph/0304176] offers a simple test statistic to study the compatibility of different data sets within a given theoretical model. papers.title: Simulation-Informed High-Velocity Dark Matter in the Effective Theory of Direct Detection
papers.abstract: The interpretation and reach of direct detection (DD) experiments depend sensitively on the local dark matter (DM) velocity distribution, particularly its high-velocity tail. This tail is crucial for elastic scattering at low DM masses or large momentum transfers, and for inelastic upscattering, where additional kinetic energy is needed to overcome the mass splitting. In practice, however, phenomenological studies typically rely either on the Standard Halo Model (SHM) or, when an enhanced high-velocity tail contributes to the scattering rate, on the single simulation that includes a large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) analogue, Au-25, whose debris reaches ~ 950\kms. In this work, we instead build on a previously presented empirically-motivated reconstruction method, to construct the local DM velocity distribution, using stellar kinematics from the Gaia space telescope. We combine this reconstructed Milky Way component with the best LMC analog in the FIRE-2 simulations, and find no local DM faster than ~ 900\kms. We compare the resulting distribution with the two commonly used benchmarks, the SHM and Au-25. We then study how these different velocity distributions affect the interpretation of DD searches across all operators of the non-relativistic effective field theory of DM--nucleon interactions, for both elastic and inelastic DM. As an illustrative application, we consider the high-energy event observed in the LUX-ZEPLIN extended search. Requiring the event to remain compatible with the absence of signal in the surrounding energy sidebands, we observe the inferred inelastic DM mass splitting can be shifted by up to $\sim 130$~keV depending on the assumed high-velocity tail. Higher-resolution simulations of the high-velocity DM population reaching the detector will therefore be crucial for interpreting a future signal and setting robust limits on DM interactions.

papers.title: Interacting quantum reference frames
papers.abstract: We formulate quantum reference frames within the Dirac quantization of gauge theories, where physical states are obtained from a kinematical Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$ by group averaging. We assume the gauge group $G$ is unimodular, and we define a quantum reference frame as a system of coherent states associated with a group $G_R$ of frame orientations acting on a tensor factor of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. In direct analogy with the Faddeev-Popov procedure in path integrals, we show that the physical inner product can be written in terms of a choice of frame orientation with an appropriate operator measure, but that the physical Hilbert space is independent of this choice of frame. This yields a generalization of the Page-Wootters reduction map used to define conditional states and conditional probabilities of measurement outcomes given a frame orientation. These probabilities correspond to the expectation values of relational Dirac observables obtained from generalizations of previously considered relativization maps. Our main result is that the map that implements a change of frame is unitary, even when $G$ does not act as a tensor-product representation across a factorization of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. The formalism therefore accommodates interactions between reference frames and the systems described relative to them. We apply this formalism to temporal frames, showing that a unitary Schrödinger equation emerges for an interacting clock and system, and that a previously reported time-nonlocal Schrödinger equation is recovered in an appropriate limit. With this, problems of non-unitarity are avoided by the use of the gauge-fixing measure in the physical inner product. We also discuss the case of interacting spatial frames, where the known correspondence between coherence in one frame and entanglement in another is shown to depend on the coupling.

papers.title: Prior volume effect inflates the gravitational-wave background in pulsar timing arrays
papers.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) have found evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background (GWB) whose amplitude exceeds most predictions based on supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs). The revised priors also yield a steeper GWB spectrum closer to the SMBHB predictions, strengthen the evidence for HD correlations, and weaken the preference for new-physics sources over SMBHBs.

papers.title: Can we constrain the binary neutron star merger time from kilonova light curves?
papers.abstract: The joint observation of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary neutron star (BNS) merger (GW170817), together with a short Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB 170817A) and a kilonova (KN, AT2017gfo), marked the birth of multimessenger astronomy with GWs, and demonstrated the informative power of multimessenger observations. More BNS merger and KN detections are expected , thanks to the increasing sensitivity of GW detectors and the advent of new electromagnetic facilities such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. However, the association between a BNS merger and a KN might not be trivial: the detection of a KN might not coincide with the onset of the EM emission, making it difficult to define a temporal window to assess the coincidence with a GW event. In this work we investigate the possibility to constrain the BNS merger time from KN light curves, exploring different observing conditions and with focus on the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. We used different KN models and different inference frameworks to simulate and fit KN light curves. We explored different cadences and wavelength coverages for observations, to investigate how the different observing conditions can affect the capability to recover the BNS merger time. The tests performed also include real data related to AT2017gfo, plus a few GRBs that have been associated to possible KN candidates. papers.title: FAUST XXXII. Chemically layered structures and ionisation in the disk and envelope of NGC 1333 IRAS 4C
papers.abstract: Recent molecular line observations with high spatial resolutions have revealed vertical chemical stratification in Class I/II disks (i.e. chemical composition changing with height in the vertical direction of the disk), as well as a radial variation of ionisation rates. However, such chemical layered structures in Class 0 disk and envelope systems have been investigated only for limited objects, such as L1527. In the context of the ALMA Large Program FAUST, we report the results of molecular line observations toward the disk and envelope around the low-mass Class 0 protostar NGC 1333 IRAS 4C in the Perseus Molecular Cloud. Previous observations have shown that the disk rotation axis of this object is largely tilted to the line of sight, making it suitable for studying the molecular abundance distribution as a function of disk height. We found that the molecules known as gas density tracers such as C18O and H2CO are distributed around the disk midplane. In addition, molecules known as tracers of photochemical reactions such as CCH and c-C3H2 are distributed in the low-density upper layers of the disk, unlike the distribution in L1527. Moreover, the column density ratio of HCO+/CO derived from the H13CO+ and C18O line emission suggests that the ionisation degree and the ionisation rate vary with the disk radius and they are larger in the outer region of the disk and envelope.

papers.title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. papers.title: Extended Local Infrared Cutoff for the Holographic Density
papers.abstract: We propose an extended local infrared cutoff for the holographic density that leads to linear cosmological equations and gives exact analytical solutions. The model allows to remove the residual matter and radiation-like terms of the local construction based on $H$ and $\dot{H}$, resulting in a clear separation between the standard cosmological fluids and the holographic sector. The homogeneous solution generates characteristic modes that give rise to different cosmological behaviors. The extension includes derivatives up to third order, where two of the characteristic modes can modify the pre-recombination expansion and reduce the sound horizon while remaining subdominant at BBN. A slightly phantom mode provides an additional late-time geometrical freedom that can further increase the CMB-compatible value of $H_0$. Optimizations using BAO constraints yield values of $H_0$ in the approximate range $70.5-72.4\ {\rm km\;s^{-1}\;Mpc^{-1}}$.

papers.title: Graviphoton mixing with KK modes in the 2D effective theory of charged black holes
papers.abstract: We study the effects of massive Kaluza--Klein modes on the two-dimensional low-energy effective theory obtained by the $S^2$ reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory on a Reissner--Nordström black hole background. The background electric flux mixes the Maxwell Kaluza--Klein scalars with the graviphotons, and tree-level exchange of the massive scalars generates a correction to the graviphoton kinetic term proportional to the square of the black hole charge. Within the leading local approximation, we also perturbatively evaluate the one-loop correction to the graviphoton kinetic term and find no dependence on the black hole charge. We find that near extremality, the charge-dependent tree-level correction becomes parametrically comparable to the classical graviphoton kinetic term.

papers.title: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r-modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: The r-modes in rotating neutron stars are a promising source of continuous gravitational waves, and may grow or be excited to amplitudes $\alpha\lesssim1$. We perform general relativistic simulations of nonlinear $l=|m|=2$ r-modes in a rapidly rotating neutron star with spin frequency $f_{spin}\approx792$ Hz, relaxing the Cowling and small-$\alpha$ approximations. The star is idealised as an unmagnetised, one-component, perfect fluid with a polytropic equation of state. The r-mode frequency is measured to be $f_{r-mode}=1014$ Hz for initial amplitude $\alpha_0=0.2$. The dimensionless frequency $\kappa\approx0.7197$ agrees with an estimate from linear perturbation theory to within 1.7%. $f_{r-mode}$ increases quadratically with amplitude, and $\kappa$ decreases by 3.4% across simulations where $\alpha_0$ is varied through the range $0.2\leq\alpha_0\leq1.2$. The gravitational wave strain calculated from the Newman-Penrose scalar implies $h_{r-mode}\approx9.7\times10^{-22}$ at $10$ kpc for $\alpha_0=0.2$, which agrees with Einstein's quadrupole formula to within 35%. We also report on nonlinear phenomena observed in our simulations, e.g. differential rotation, amplitude decay, and signatures of nonlinear mode coupling in the spacetime oscillations.

papers.title: simesh: A Python Framework for Quantitative Analysis of Native AMR Data from MPI-AMRVAC
papers.abstract: Adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) is widely used in large-scale astrophysical simulations, but the resulting multilevel data are challenging to analyze quantitatively. We present simesh, an independent Python framework for quantitative analysis of cell-centered fields on block-structured AMR meshes. The current implementation targets three-dimensional Cartesian datasets from MPI-AMRVAC and compatible AGILE snapshots, preserving the native AMR hierarchy and connecting complementary scientific diagnostics within a common numerical representation. The framework combines Python workflow interfaces with compiled Cython kernels, supporting efficient analysis on AMR meshes. We compare native AMR analysis with a VTK point-data conversion and uniform-grid resampling, which shows that changes in data association, interpolation support, and differentiation scale affect both sampled magnetic fields and derived current densities. Small differences in the sampled primary field can become more pronounced in derivative-based quantities, particularly near coarse-fine interfaces. The applications combine field diagnostics, tracing, regional statistics, and line-of-sight integration on the same native AMR representation. simesh makes these operations available through reusable Python interfaces for reproducible analysis of multiscale simulation data.

papers.title: Lasting mEMRIs: Signatures of Multiple Black Hole Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals from AGN discs
papers.abstract: Encounters of stellar-mass black holes (sBH) in active galactic nuclei discs naturally form mean-motion resonances of sBH pairs. These mean-motion resonances can be broken close to the central supermassive black hole when gravitational-wave emission dominates over gas torques. We derive a simple condition that depends only on the sBH mass ratio and the resonance index for which a pair of sBH in a mean-motion resonance will remain intact and can be detectable as a multiple Extreme-Mass-Ratio-Inspirals (mEMRIs) in the LISA band. We present for the first time the gravitational-wave strain signatures of a pair of co-migrating sBH in mean-motion resonance, including additional gravitational-wave harmonics associated with orbital conjunctions of the individual EMRIs. The frequency evolution and the associated chirp mass is degenerate with isolated EMRIs of different masses. However, the mEMRI mass ratio is quantised by the resonance order and is larger than the true mass ratio. The degeneracy can be broken if the true sBH mass ratio can be inferred from individual strain amplitudes. We argue that mEMRIs should be common if disc driven EMRIs are to be detected by LISA, with $\sim 10$ mEMRIs per year in the local universe ($z \lesssim 0.2$), highlighting the need to model mEMRI systems in future LISA data analysis.

papers.title: Domain models of turbulent magnetic fields and the spectral shape of ensemble averaged axion-photon conversion
papers.abstract: Axion-like particles are light pseudoscalars that appear in many extensions of the Standard Model and are candidates for dark matter. Through their mixing with photons, they imprint energy dependent modulations on the spectra of astrophysical sources shining through magnetised media. When a distant source shines through the turbulent magnetic field of an intervening galaxy cluster, these modulations are stochastic. It has recently been shown that averaging over an ensemble of such sources instead produces a smooth absorption-like feature. In this work we derive the analytic form of this ensemble averaged signal, previously known only numerically. We further relate the index $a$ of the magnetic field energy spectrum to the index $\beta$ of the domain size distribution that simulations use to describe the turbulent field. For $1<a<2$ the two indices obey the simple analytic relation $\beta=3-a$. Any distribution with $\beta<1$ instead mimics the spectral index $a=2$, which the sharp domain walls impose. For Kolmogorov turbulence, relevant for galaxy clusters, the relation gives $\beta=4/3$.

papers.title: Stellar Loci X: Selection of Nitrogen-Rich Giants Using GALEX NUV and Synthetic SDSS Photometry
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-rich (N-rich) field stars (likely second-generation escapees from globular clusters) provide a powerful, but currently sample-limited, probe of globular-cluster disruption in the Galactic halo. We exploit the fact that enhanced NH, CN absorption depresses optical u band flux, while the near-ultraviolet (NUV) band is largely insensitive to nitrogen enhancement while remaining sensitive to overall metallicity. Combining GALEX NUV photometry with (synthetic) SDSS optical photometry, we construct a [Fe/H]-dependent stellar-locus model for giants and select significant redder u-g outliers as N-rich candidates. For a relaxed cut ([Fe/H] <= -0.8, 2 sigma) we identify 970 candidates, with an estimated completeness of 64-65% and purity of 41-62% from multiple validations. A stricter selection ([Fe/H] <= -1.0, 3 sigma) yields 220 candidates, with lower completeness (30-38%) but substantially higher purity (60-91%). The dominant contaminants show anomalous spectral energy distributions (e.g., UV excess), and are themselves useful targets for follow-up. The diverse kinematic and dynamical properties of our candidates suggest multiple origins. This scalable photometric approach enables systematic searches for N-rich halo stars and is well suited to forthcoming wide-field surveys such as CSST.

papers.title: Scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety
papers.abstract: The unitarity and causality properties of asymptotically safe quantum gravity are still unsettled. Scattering amplitudes provide a direct test, but their computation requires fully momentum-dependent correlation functions. In this light, we compute the full scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety within a mostly analytic approximation. Qualitatively, we find the expected logarithmic branch-cut structure, and we correctly recover the double-eikonal soft divergences predicted by Weinberg's soft theorem. Quantitatively, we find that non-minimal operators are generally as important as the minimal vertex stemming from the scalar kinetic term.

papers.title: On Particle Production from Bubble Collisions in the Non-runaway Regime
papers.abstract: Particle production from bubble collisions during First-Order Phase Transitions (FOPTs) has been studied as an efficient mechanism for baryogenesis and dark matter production, but existing semi-analytical treatments assume runaway bubbles with wall velocity $v_w\to 1$. We generalize this treatment to arbitrary $v_w< 1$, relevant for scenarios such as electroweak baryogenesis and transitions with significant wall friction. We first extend the analytical trapping-equation approach to finite-thickness boosted kink profiles for both elastic and inelastic collisions, then go beyond this by numerically solving the full Klein-Gordon equation without assuming $SO(1,1)$ symmetry or thin walls, across a broad grid of $v_w$ and potential shapes. We find the analytical generalization underestimates the true efficiency factor by orders of magnitude away from $v_w\to 1$, and provide new semi-analytic fit functions consisting of a power-law continuum plus a resonance peak, which reproduce the main spectral features of the numerical results across the parameter range studied. Applying these to a toy dark sector model, we show particle production is strongly suppressed as $v_w$ decreases from unity, enhanced for lighter produced particles, and that the relative contribution from the oscillatory peak differs from prior runaway-regime estimates. We also discuss limitations of the trapping equation and the off-shell effective-action truncation underlying this formalism.

papers.title: A signature of the timelike singularity in holography
papers.abstract: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, we provide a simple observable, the imaginary part of the retarded Green's function, which captures the timelike singularity of a charged black brane. These contributions admit an interpretation in terms of paths in an analytically continued classical black brane interior via a WKB approximation: they provide the complex time elapsed along null geodesics that reflect off the singularity, and incorporate the corresponding reflection coefficients.

papers.title: Quantum mechanical Gaussian wavepackets of single relativistic particles
papers.abstract: We study the evolutions of selected quasi-(1+1) dimensional wavepacket solutions to the Klein-Gordon equation for a relativistic charged particle in uniform motion or accelerated by a uniform electric field in Minkowski space. We find that the minimal initial width of a wavepacket for a good Gaussian approximation in position space is about the Compton wavelength of the particle divided by its Lorentz factor at the initial moment. This can be considered as a manifestation of relativistic length contraction, which is also observed numerically in the spreading of the wavepacket's charge density.

papers.title: Local uniqueness of the Black String with small circle size
papers.abstract: In this article we study uniqueness of the Black String, i.e. the product of 4-dimensional Schwarzschild space with a circle of length L. In arXiv:2410.20967, this was reduced to a non-linear elliptic PDE, and we use this setup to show that for small L the Black String is infinitesimally rigid as a Ricci-flat metric. Using a fixed point theorem, we prove that this implies local uniqueness, i.e. there exist no other Ricci-flat metrics near the Black String, and we give bounds for the size of the neighborhood in which the Black String is unique. We compare this with the toy problem of a scalar field satisfying an elliptic equation that was already solved in arXiv:2410.20967 using different methods. In this case we can use the fixed point theorem method to prove not just a local but a global statement.

papers.title: Cauchy-horizon flux coefficients in the reduced Polyakov model
papers.abstract: We study Cauchy-horizon flux amplification in the stationary reduced Polyakov model for spherically symmetric charged black holes. The corresponding four-dimensional coefficient depends on global scattering and on the quantum state, while the reduced model gives an exactly calculable anomaly-induced radial contribution. For a nonextremal inner horizon on a stationary background, a finite late-time Eddington--Finkelstein flux is amplified by the affine blueshift into a leading $V_-^{-2}$ divergence. In the Polyakov model the coefficient is $F_-^{(\infty)}=t_v-N\kappa_-^2/(48\pi)$, so the leading term vanishes only when $t_v=N\kappa_-^2/(48\pi)$. This inner-horizon condition is distinct from the corresponding outer-horizon condition on $t_u$, while standard Unruh-type and outer-horizon thermal choices generically lie away from it. Other quantum contributions and classical tails enter through the total late-time flux. Cancellation of the $V_-^{-2}$ term requires the total constant coefficient $F_0$ to vanish, while asymptotically flat power-law tails produce logarithmically weakened divergences and exponentially decaying de~Sitter tails produce a different power of $V_-$. These results identify the conditions controlling the leading Cauchy-horizon divergence and its cancellation.

papers.title: Anatomy of RHN DM relic in the vanilla scotogenic neutrino mass model
papers.abstract: The scotogeneic neutrino mass models are very popular choices to generate light neutrino masses via radiative mechanism. In these models, the particles running in the loop are distinguished from the standard model due to an imposed $\mathcal{Z}_2$ symmetry under which the loop particles are odd. Therefore, the lightest particle running in the loop can be a viable dark matter candidate. In this paper, we revisit the minimal scotogenic neutrino mass model and study the anatomy of right handed neutrino (RHN) DM relic, taking into account contributions from self-annihilation, co-annihilation, conversion-driven processes, as well as production via the freeze-in mechanism. We impose the constraints from direct detection and collider searches of DM including anomalous magnetic moment of muon, charged lepton flavor violation and low-energy neutrino oscillation data to show that the lightest RHN can be a viable DM in the mass range: $M_{h}/2\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim2000 {\rm GeV}$ (thermal DM) and $0.1 ~{\rm GeV}\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim 1000 {\rm GeV}$ (non-thermal DM), where $M_h$ denotes the Standard Model Higgs mass and $M_{\rm DM}$ is the RHN dark matter mass. We also find the displaced vertex signatures of long lived particles which can be probed at future colliders.

papers.title: Recovering 3D Magnetic Turbulence from Single-frequency Faraday Screens
papers.abstract: Statistics of polarized synchrotron radiation carry information about the properties of the underlying turbulence. We consider a setup in which synchrotron radiation is emitted in a distant volume and then passes through a turbulent screen that induces Faraday rotation. Using both MHD simulations and synthetic turbulence spectra, we explore the spectrum of observed polarization directions measured at a single frequency as a diagnostic for recovering the statistics of turbulence in both the emitting region and the Faraday rotation volume. We compare these results with our analytical expectations. In doing so, we compare the directional spectrum with the wavelength-derivative diagnostic explored earlier by Lazarian & Pogosyan. We demonstrate that the directional spectrum exhibits greater sensitivity to the turbulence in the Faraday rotation volume. We provide an observer-friendly criterion to determine whether it samples turbulence in the synchrotron-emitting region or in the Faraday rotation region. These results open a practical pathway for extracting turbulence statistics from existing and forthcoming single-band radio polarimetry.

papers.title: Impact of non-standard neutrino-electron interactions on Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
papers.abstract: Neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) with electrons, predicted in many extended theoretical models of particle physics, are known to alter the picture of neutrino decoupling from the cosmic plasma. We update previous analyses of neutrino decoupling in the presence of NSI with electrons, extending the parameter space and assessing their impact on the primordial light-element abundances produced during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN). We show that tracking the NSI-induced modifications of the neutrino distributions is necessary to accurately predict the helium-4 abundance, which cannot be derived from a pure $N_{\rm eff}$-driven change. BBN therefore provides additional observables that are complementary to $N_{\rm eff}$. We then derive cosmological constraints on non-universal and flavour-changing NSI parameters, using different dataset combinations, and compare them with bounds from terrestrial experiments. We find that the cosmological limits are significantly less stringent than the terrestrial ones, but they provide an independent probe of neutrino interactions in the early universe.

papers.title: Diversity in Lyman Continuum Escape at $z\sim0.3$ Revealed by WISE Infrared Observations
papers.abstract: The escape of Lyman continuum (LyC) radiation from star-forming galaxies plays a key role in cosmic reionization. While strong LyC leakers are commonly identified through ultraviolet (UV) and optical diagnostics, their infrared (IR) emission remains poorly explored. We use data from the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) to investigate a sample of local star-forming galaxies, which contains 20 strong LyC leakers ($S/N_\mathrm{LyC} > 3$ and $f_{\rm esc}>5\%$) and 69 non-leakers. Among the strong leakers, 8 are classified with mid-IR detections. Comparing the IR-detected and IR-undetected subsamples, we find that the IR-undetected strong leakers exhibit higher [\ion{O}{3}]5007/[\ion{O}{2}]3726,3729 (O32) ratios, bluer UV slopes, and lower metallicities than the other subsamples. In contrast, the IR-detected strong leakers show O32 ratios, UV slopes, and metallicities comparable to those of non-leakers, while maintaining a median escape fraction of $f_{\rm esc}\sim12\%$. These results indicate that significant LyC escape is not limited to galaxies with the most extreme UV and optical properties and can coexist with substantial IR emission. The Ly$\alpha$ profiles and the morphology of the IR-detected and IR-undetected strong leakers imply that LyC photon escape in these two classes may be driven by different mechanisms. Our results highlight the diversity of LyC leakers and suggest that dusty star-forming galaxies may contribute a considerable amount to the ionizing photon budget during cosmic reionization.

papers.title: ML in Astrophysical Turbulence I: Predicting Prestellar Cores in Magnetized Molecular Clouds using eXtreme Gradient Boosting
papers.abstract: Giant Molecular Clouds (GMCs) are dominated by supersonic turbulence and magnetic fields, creating a complex network of shocks and filaments that regulate star formation, making it challenging to predict which individual gas parcels will collapse into star-forming cores. Here, we present an XGBoost machine learning framework to forecast the 3D Lagrangian trajectories and gravitational collapse fate of prestellar gas. Models were trained on $\sim 2.1$ million tracer particles from self-gravitating, turbulent magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations. By mapping instantaneous point-wise states (position, velocity, density, and magnetic fields) to future coordinates, our regression model predicts continuous 3D spatial evolution over $0.25~t_{\rm ff}$ ($\approx 0.31\text{ Myr}$) with $R^2 > 0.99$. Concurrently, our classifier accurately ranks gravitational core susceptibility ($\text{AUC} = 0.975$). Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we interpret the model's decision hierarchy, revealing that local density, kinetic energy, and magnetic field magnitude dominate core identification. SHAP dependence analysis shows that the model re-derives a sharp non-linear collapse threshold at $\log_{10}\rho \approx 0.8$ above which magnetic fields amplify collapse predictions. The classification task reveals a conservative false-positive rate (37% precision) at absolute binary thresholds. We demonstrate that while point-wise ML models excel at kinematic advection, they mathematically lack the spatial context required to evaluate local differential operators (such as magnetic directional derivatives, thermal pressure gradients, or field curvature) that are physically necessary to stop collapse. This data-driven approach offers a computationally efficient foundation for advective subgrid modeling while highlighting the necessity of spatial architectures to establish absolute core-formation criteria.

papers.title: Deep Learning Search for Gravitational Waves from Compact Binary Coalescence
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave searches rely on a combination of methods, including matched filtering, coherent analyses, and more recent machine-learning-based pipelines. For compact binary coalescences --- where signals originate from the relativistic dynamics of compact objects --- matched filtering remains a central element, but its computational cost will increase substantially with the data volumes and parameter-space coverage required by next-generation interferometers such as the Einstein Telescope. Developing complementary strategies that reduce computational load while preserving detection performance is therefore essential. We investigate a hybrid approach that combines matched-filtering concepts with Convolutional Neural Networks, enabling efficient signal searches without relying on the usual $\chi^2$ rejection test. Using simulated data sets that include injected signals in Gaussian noise, transient noise, and physical effects not represented in the template bank --- such as eccentricity, precession and higher-order modes --- we show that the method achieves a detection efficiency comparable to or better than a standard matched-filtering search while offering a more resource-efficient pipeline in all the cases where the physics included in the signals were not represented in the template bank or when glitches were affecting the data. Conversely, the analysis also reveals some loss of detection capability for standard BNS/BBH searches in pure Gaussian noise. These results indicate that deep-learning-assisted searches can support sustainable gravitational-wave data analysis in future detector eras.

papers.title: Ridged Lagrangian Perturbation Theory (RLPT)
papers.abstract: Galaxy surveys demand fast large-scale structure forward models that preserve large-scale phases while providing realistic nonlinear morphology at fixed force resolution. Single-step Lagrangian Perturbation Theory (LPT) solvers are efficient, but they typically yield overly diffuse filaments and knots and underpredict small-scale clustering. We introduce Ridged Lagrangian Perturbation Theory (RLPT), a modular two-step scheme: a standard long-range LPT/ALPT transport is followed by a single post-processing Eulerian ridging update that reconstructs a short-range, curl-free displacement from the realised density field through a smooth scale separation and a Poisson inversion. This explicit completion layer is inexpensive, preserves the large-scale solution, and provides a small set of transparent parameters to tune the short-range response. We test RLPT against particle-mesh and $N$-body references and find that one additional ridging step systematically improves both nonlinear power and field-level agreement relative to 2LPT/ALPT baselines. Finally, we demonstrate that ridging can be repurposed as a deterministic subgrid relocation model: even when the underlying dark-matter field is only "good enough" on the mesh, ridging enables controlled tuning of tracer clustering beyond the nominal resolution, which is particularly relevant for mock-galaxy production and observational systematics sensitive to close pairs.

papers.title: Calibrating optical galaxy cluster projection effects with sparse spectroscopic samples: A clustering redshift approach
papers.abstract: Wide-field optical imaging surveys are efficient at identifying galaxy clusters, but optically identified clusters suffer from projection effects---physically unassociated galaxies along the line of sight are often included as cluster members due to distance uncertainties. Previous studies have used spectroscopic follow-up observations of cluster members to quantify projection effects; however, such follow-up efforts cannot keep pace with the rapidly growing cluster samples. On the other hand, spectroscopic surveys designed for large-scale structure studies collect tens of millions of spectra but tend to have sparse spectra in cluster regions. To bridge this gap, we develop a clustering redshift approach that cross-correlates cluster members with sparse, noncluster-targeted spectroscopic galaxy samples. We validate this approach using the Cardinal simulation, recovering the correct spectroscopic redshift distribution and projection effect parameters of cluster members identified by the red-sequence Matched-filter Probabilistic Percolation algorithm. Our approach is insensitive to the selection of the spectroscopic sample and paves the way for calibrating projection effects in the upcoming Legacy Survey of Space and Time clusters using DESI and Roman spectroscopic samples.

papers.title: The missing ultra-faint satellites of the Milky Way
papers.abstract: We combine the highest resolution N-body simulation of a $\sim10^{12}M_\odot$ $\Lambda$CDM halo (Aquarius-A) with the semi-analytic model GALFORM to study the full satellite population of Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies. The model assumes that galaxies form only in subhalos whose peak circular velocity exceeds the hydrogen-cooling threshold, and predicts that the total number of satellites ever accreted into the main halo, down to arbitrarily low luminosity, should not exceed a few hundred. The model tracks satellites even after their halos become unresolved ("orphan" galaxies), and includes a novel treatment of dark matter and stellar tidal stripping which takes into account that $\Lambda$CDM subhalos survive tidal disruption because of their cuspy density profiles. Our results match the massive end of the observed MW satellite mass function and predict that many ultra-faint dwarfs (UFDs) with $M_V>-5$ are missing from the current MW satellite census. The missing UFDs are predicted to avoid the innermost regions of the host, and have properties overlapping those of the recently-discovered ultra-faint compact MW satellites (UFCSs). If the faintest dwarfs are initially as compact as UFCSs, our results suggest that many UFCSs should be dark matter-dominated dwarfs with velocity dispersions $1-3$ km/s which survived disruption because they inhabit the cusp of $\Lambda$CDM subhalos. UFCSs have predicted densities of $10^{10}$-$10^{11}\,M_\odot/$kpc$^3$, higher than those of more extended UFDs. If confirmed, our results provide strong support for the cuspy nature of $\Lambda$CDM halos and for the hydrogen-cooling threshold for galaxy formation.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 15 figures. Version accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.title: JOYS: Launch and destruction of dust in protostellar jets. The case of BHR71-IRS1 with JWST MIRI
papers.abstract: Protostellar winds can theoretically lift solids from the planet-forming disks, but direct evidence for launched dust has been scarce so far. Numerous atomic lines that are unique to mid-infrared (IR) wavelengths reveal refractories eroded from dust grains and provide information on wind properties in the earliest stages of the star formation process. We present JWST MIRI-MRS spectral imaging of the inner 2000 au of the BHR71-IRS1 blueshifted side of the outflow. Atomic line intensities are compared to shock models to constrain the physical conditions and elemental abundances of the outflowing gas. Dust continuum maps were constructed from PSF-subtracted cubes, and the spectral energy distribution of the dust was analyzed. The ionized central jet of BHR71-IRS1 is spatially resolved and imaged for the first time, revealing a unique inventory of refractory, volatile, and noble-gas fine-structure lines (Fe, Ni, Co, Cl, S, Ne, Ar). The emission is concentrated along four bright knots that wiggle along the jet axis. PSF-subtracted continuum maps reveal extended mid-IR continuum emission co-spatial with the jet bullets and within the H$_2$-traced outflow cone. Spectral energy distributions along the jet are fit together with the extinction, revealing a warm (200-400 K) and a cold (70-90 K) dust component. The shock modeling constrained by the mid-IR lines indicates a decline in the shock velocity from 70 to 35 km s$^{-1}$ and in the pre-shock density from $>$10$^5$ to $ 4\times 10^4$ cm$^{-3}$ with distance from the protostar. Gas-phase Fe and Ni are measurably depleted relative to Solar abundances, consistent with a substantial fraction of refractories remaining locked in grains in spite of the shocks. These JWST observations provide direct evidence that dust is launched in a Class 0 jet and at least partly survives shock processing.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 23 figures, accepted for publication in the Astronomy and Astrophysics

papers.title: Decrease of the entanglement entropy of the Hawking radiation induced by backreaction in the Bose-Einstein condensate
papers.abstract: We analytically study the effect of backreaction from analog Hawking radiation on its entanglement entropy in the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). The backreaction is expected to play an essential role in the decrease of the entanglement entropy and in realizing the Page curve. Since the BEC theory has microscopic Hamiltonian and thus exhibits unitarity, it is desirable to reproduce the Page curve explicitly by using the Hamiltonian. As the first step towards this goal, we concretely study the BEC with a step-like configuration that has been extensively studied in the literature. By using the microscopic theory, we derive an explicit form of backreaction from analog Hawking radiation. Combining it with the known results of the Bogoliubov coefficients, we analytically compute the entanglement entropy of the Hawking radiation, and show that the backreaction reduces the growth of the entanglement entropy as expected for sufficiently low energy modes over a wide range of the parameter characterizing the step-like configuration.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Phase Transitions in Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
papers.abstract: Although asymptotically flat black holes generically lack thermodynamic phase transitions, we show that curvature-induced scalarization of electrically charged black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory provides a natural setting for nontrivial thermodynamic behavior, without invoking external confining mechanisms or an extended thermodynamic formalism. Working within the canonical ensemble and employing the Euclidean approach, we identify the coexistence of locally stable scalarized and Reissner-Nordström thermal states, which promotes free-energy crossings to bona fide phase transitions between equilibrium phases. For weak coupling, a second-order phase transition coincides with the second bifurcation point, at which the scalarized branch reconnects with the Reissner-Nordström branch and scalar hair is spontaneously shed. As the coupling strength increases, this transition becomes zeroth order, the scalarized branch shrinks, and a fish-like structure develops in its Helmholtz free energy, rendering locally stable thermal states partially metastable, and yielding up to three phase transitions. In the strong-coupling limit, the scalarized branch reduces to a Schwarzschild-like solution, and the Reissner-Nordström phase ultimately emerges as the sole thermodynamically preferred configuration.

papers.title: Stardust Galaxies at z>9: A Dust-Origin Transition Behind the Excess of UV-Bright Galaxies
papers.abstract: Recent JWST observations suggest that galaxies at z > 9 may be dominated by low-opacity SNe-produced dust before efficient ISM grain growth is established. This transition in dust origin and opacity could explain both the prevalence of galaxies with extremely low dust attenuation and the excess of UV-bright galaxies relative to most pre-JWST predictions. We investigate whether this transition, combined with evolving star-formation efficiency, can reproduce these observed properties. We develop a physically motivated attenuation framework combining (i) extinction laws for reverse-shock-processed SNe dust, (ii) metallicity- and dust-to-metal-dependent opacity scalings, and (iii) porous radiative-transfer geometries allowing partial UV-photon leakage. Unlike outflow-driven scenarios requiring large-scale gas evacuation, our approach preserves gas reservoirs while reducing effective UV opacity through dust composition and geometry. We introduce extinction-based, gas-based, and hybrid attenuation prescriptions linking SNe-dominated and ISM grain-growth dust regimes. We find that the observed A_FUV-M_star relation at z > 9 is best reproduced for an intrinsic FUV dust opacity kappa_UV(dust)=10^3 - 10^4 cm2/g, characteristic of low-opacity SNe dust, naturally producing very low attenuation even in gas-rich galaxies. This regime reproduces galaxies with extremely low dust attenuation (GELDAs), which dominate observed samples at z > 9. Applied to intrinsic UV luminosity function models, our SNe-dominated and hybrid prescriptions mainly suppress the brightest galaxies, bringing predictions into agreement with JWST measurements without requiring extreme star-formation efficiencies or dust-free interstellar media. Our results suggest that the UV-bright galaxy excess at z > 9 reflects a transition in dust origin and opacity during the earliest phases of galaxy evolution.

papers.title: Testing Black Holes with Interstellar Missions: I. Orbiting Probes
papers.abstract: Recently, we showed that the possibility of an interstellar mission to the closest black hole, while highly speculative and extremely challenging, is not completely unrealistic within the next few decades. Since such a mission might last around a century and require significant financial and human resources, it is crucial to assess whether it can truly study black holes and test General Relativity at levels unattainable by observational facilities in the Solar System for many years. In this manuscript, we assume the capability to decelerate the spacecraft and present a preliminary study of how probes orbiting a black hole could test the nature of the compact object.

papers.title: A Unified HI Rotation Curve Database for 122 Dwarf and Irregular Galaxies
papers.abstract: We present a unified HI rotation curve database for 122 dwarf and irregular galaxies drawn from three Local Volume surveys, the Local Volume HI Survey (LVHIS; 32 galaxies), VLA-ANGST (29) and LITTLE THINGS (26), and from the WALLABY DR2 kinematic catalogue (35). The database provides standardised kinematic parameters, distance estimates, morphological classifications, and rotation curve data in machine-readable JSON, JSONL, and CSV formats with a documented schema, supporting retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications and cross-survey kinematic analysis. Quality tiers distinguish 26 galaxies with published tilted-ring rotation curves and per-point uncertainties from 96 automated-pipeline, single-ring or profile-width entries. Three worked examples demonstrate corpus queries, including evaluation of the $\omega$ estimator for DDO 154 (LITTLE THINGS). This work is presented as a data resource; no new dynamical model is proposed. This version describes corpus v1.3, which corrects the LITTLE THINGS curves (v1.1), the WALLABY entries (v1.2) and the LVHIS entries and reference (v1.3) of v1.0. The database and all computation scripts are available at Zenodo (this https URL).

papers.title: Signals from the early Universe: a comprehensive search for primordial features in Planck CMB datasets
papers.abstract: We investigate the presence of primordial oscillatory features in measurements of CMB anisotropies through a systematic comparison of phenomenological templates. Building upon previous searches for primordial features using Planck data, we compare the full PR3 legacy release with the PR4 (NPIPE) processing to assess how the results depend on the choice of CMB maps and likelihood framework. To maximise our sensitivity to rapidly varying oscillatory signals, we employ unbinned likelihoods. We find that several previously reported indications of oscillatory structure persist across different analyses, although none attains global statistical significance. Furthermore, some anomalies reported in earlier studies are substantially reduced when updated to the new versions of the CamSpec likelihood using Planck PR4 products. For all templates considered, we identify a small number of frequencies in the range $\omega \sim 10-100$ that improve the fit to the CMB data by up to $\Delta\chi^2 \simeq -10$ to $-15$ relative to the featureless reference model. However, this improvement is not supported by a Bayesian model comparison. The inclusion of three or four additional parameters can reduces the overall predictability of the feature models and leads to an Occam penalty. Finally, after properly accounting for the look-elsewhere effect, the significance of the preferred frequencies is reduced, corresponding to a global statistical significance of at most $2.6\sigma$. We present forecasts for forthcoming CMB experiments, highlighting the decisive role of next-generation polarisation measurements in distinguishing genuine primordial oscillations from statistical fluctuations and modelling systematics. The upper bounds or uncertainties on the feature amplitudes, expected from the combination of SO and LiteBIRD, improve by more than one order of magnitude.

papers.title: Ellis-Bronnikov Wormhole Shadows with Spherically Symmetric Accretion Flow
papers.abstract: We investigate the observational differences between the Ellis--Bronnikov (EB) wormhole and the Schwarzschild black hole (BH) by performing general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) simulations. We consider a spherically symmetric steady-state accretion flow and perform GRRT simulations incorporating synchrotron emission. For both the EB wormhole and the Schwarzschild BH, the simulated images consist of a central shadow region and a bright photon ring. We find that both the shadow region and the photon ring of the EB wormhole are brighter than those of the Schwarzschild BH. These differences arise from the absence of an event horizon in the EB wormhole, allowing the emission from the accreting matter around and beyond the throat to contribute to the intensity. We also compare the simulated images with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observations of M87*. Although the total flux and the ring diameter are comparable with the EHT results, our models with the spherically symmetric accretion flow cannot reproduce the deep central brightness depression observed by the EHT, for both the EB wormhole and the Schwarzschild BH. This indicates that a non-spherical accretion flow is required for a detailed comparison with the EHT image.

papers.title: The role of major mergers in triggering super-Eddington accretion
papers.abstract: JWST observations have opened a new era in the exploration of the high-redshift Universe, revealing black holes (BHs) with masses of several million solar masses already at $z>8$, challenging our understanding of their growth mechanisms. In this context, super-Eddington (SE) accretion has emerged as a promising solution and has been widely adopted in both numerical simulations and semi-analytical models. In this work, we investigate whether a major merger between two relatively low-mass halos ($M_{\rm halo}\sim10^9\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$) at high redshift can trigger episodes of sustained SE accretion, with particular focus on the role of BH feedback. We employ state-of-the-art, high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of a major merger at $z\sim11$. We explore different prescriptions for BH seeding and feedback, including physically motivated radiative and kinetic models (winds and jets) across the three main accretion regimes: advection-dominated accretion flows (ADAF), radiatively efficient sub-Eddington accretion, and SE accretion. For the relatively low-mass halos studied here, our feedback prescription efficiently suppresses gas accretion, preventing substantial BH growth. We find that, although the merger drives gas inflows towards the central regions, this is not sufficient to trigger sustained SE accretion. Post-merger SE accretion episodes are observed only when BH feedback is entirely switched off. Amongst the feedback channels considered, kinetic feedback is the primary mechanism regulating BH growth. Moreover, the only significant SE accretion episodes occur immediately after BH seeding, while the merger itself does not produce a substantial enhancement of the accretion rate.
papers.comments: 12+2 pages, 8 figures; accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)

papers.title: Black hole populations and hierarchical growth across the AGN parameter space
papers.abstract: Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have been proposed as efficient environments for the formation of binary black holes (BBHs). We present an updated semi-analytical framework for BBH formation and evolution in AGN disks, following the capture, migration, pair-up, gas-driven hardening, binary--single encounters, and merger of stellar-origin black holes. We systematically explore the dependence of the resulting BBH merger population on the main AGN parameters, namely the supermassive black hole mass $M_\bullet$, the Eddington ratio $\lambda_\bullet$, and the disk viscosity parameter $\alpha$, and construct an intrinsic BBH population by weighting the simulations according to observed low-redshift AGN properties. We find that AGN disks can produce repeated mergers and build a high-mass tail extending beyond the pair-instability mass gap and into the intermediate-mass range. Hierarchical growth is more efficient in lower-viscosity disks, with $\alpha=0.01$, while higher-viscosity disks suppress the formation of massive remnants. The merger efficiency generally increases with $\lambda_\bullet$, but its dependence on $M_\bullet$ is non-trivial. The AGN-assisted BBH population is characterized by increasingly unequal mass ratios at high primary mass, a correlation between primary mass and $|\chi_{\rm eff}|$, and an effective-spin distribution that depends strongly on the fraction of binaries born in prograde or retrograde configurations. We find that the AGN channel can reproduce systems broadly consistent with the massive BBH events GW190521 and GW231123. We test several variations of the physical model, including different formalisms for migration torques, gas hardening, and three-body encounters. The general properties of the population are robust across these variations, with the high-mass tail and spin signatures persisting in all cases except when gas hardening is switched off.

papers.title: The Lifecycle and Emission Properties of PAHs in Cosmological Hydrodynamic Galaxy Formation Simulations
papers.abstract: We present the first cosmological model for the lifecycle and luminous properties of PAHs in galaxies as they evolve from z=6-->0. We model 40 zoom-in galaxies, coupled with an on-the-fly model for the evolution of dust grains in the ISM. We approximate PAHs as ultrasmall (a < 13 Angstrom) carbonaceous dust grains, and couple this model with single-photon excitation calculations to compute the emergent mid-infrared spectra. (1) If we assume that dust is large upon formation, then PAHs are naturally able to form in situ in the ISM via grain-grain shattering. Interstellar collision velocities increase in low density, diffuse gas in our model; as galaxies evolve, the increase in fractional mass of diffuse gas drives an increase in grain-grain collision velocities and a corresponding rise in the PAH mass fraction (qPAH) from ~5 x 10^{-4} at z~4 to ~10^{-2} at z~0. (2) Increased PAH production in the diffuse ISM results in an inverse relationship between qPAH and the molecular gas fraction. (3) The PAH light-to-mass ratio scales linearly with the radiation field intensity (LPAH/MPAH ~ G_0) but anti-correlates with qPAH, because high-Sigma_SFR galaxies have a denser ISM that suppresses shattering. This means the physical qPAH and observed LPAH/LFIR do not evolve in lockstep. (4) The PAH-metallicity relationship (PZR) arises naturally in this framework: galaxies enrich and grow their diffuse ISM fraction simultaneously, linking rising metallicity to rising qPAH. Our models represent the first to reproduce the PZR observed across z=0-2. (5) The LPAH-SFR and LPAH-M_mol relations emerge from two effects: more massive galaxies have larger PAH reservoirs, and higher-SFR galaxies excite their PAHs more efficiently per unit mass. Taken together, these results suggest that grain-grain shattering in the diffuse ISM is the main driver behind the evolution of cosmic PAH abundances.
papers.comments: Published in the Open Journal of Astrophysics

papers.title: Primordial black hole formation in bulk-viscous cosmology
papers.abstract: We investigate primordial black hole (PBH) formation in a cosmological background with bulk viscosity. Using numerical simulations, we determine the collapse threshold and the resulting PBH mass. We find that the critical threshold $\mu_c$ retains a dependence on the equation-of-state parameter $w$ similar to that in the inviscid case, but is enhanced by an amount comparable to the bulk-viscosity strength $\epsilon$. For fixed $w$, the increase in $\mu_c$ is approximately linear in $\epsilon$. By fitting the standard critical-scaling law for near-threshold collapse, we find that the bulk viscosity leads to an enhancement in the resulting PBH mass. These results indicate that bulk viscosity can systematically modify both the PBH threshold and PBH mass scaling law in the early Universe.

papers.title: Ultralight dark matter mixed with primordial black holes
papers.abstract: Dark matter candidates span many orders of magnitude in mass, from ultralight bosonic fields to massive compact objects. In this work, we connect these two extremes by investigating ultralight dark matter (ULDM) mixed with primordial black holes (PBHs). We study mixed ULDM-PBH halos by separating the continuum PBH contribution from the shot-noise fluctuation generated by discrete PBHs. The continuum contribution enters the averaged Schrödinger-Poisson background, while the discreteness contribution is treated as a perturbation that induces ULDM eigenmode transitions and soliton heating. The two contributions have distinct parametric dependencies: continuum effects scale with PBH fraction, whereas discreteness-driven transition rates scale with the product of PBH fraction and individual PBH mass in the perturbative regime. For a fiducial mixed halo with ULDM particle mass $10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}$, virial mass of order $10^{10}\,M_{\odot}$, and PBH fraction $1\%$, the continuum PBH component modifies the background density, gravitational potential, and low-lying ULDM eigenvalues only at the sub-percent level. Nevertheless, this percent-level continuum PBH contribution produces a tens-of-percent response in the coherent soliton region, changing the radial mode participation by about $20\%$. For stellar-mass PBHs, the discrete shot-noise fluctuation induces extremely slow ULDM mode transitions, with the fastest low-lying multiplet transition having a timescale of order $10^9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ for solar-mass PBHs. In this regime, the leading PBH effect is the continuum contribution, while discrete PBH shot noise is dynamically negligible on galactic timescales.

papers.title: The Stellar "Snake"-V: the census within 3 kpc in the Solar Neighborhood
papers.abstract: We present a Gaia DR3 source-level catalogue of Stellar Snake complexes within 3 kpc of the Sun. We define a Stellar Snake as a mutually coherent association of stellar overdensities, characterised by consistent positions, kinematics, orbital invariants, and ages, rather than a single gravitationally bound object. Moving beyond catalogue searches seeded by known open clusters, our framework operates directly on Gaia sources to recover extended, low-density substructures and interconnecting stellar bridges. The multi-stage pipeline extracts statistically significant, non-overlapping base nodes, infers homogeneous parameters using a PointNet point-cloud regressor, and links these nodes into large-scale macro-structures in a nine-coordinate feature space spanning positions, velocities, age log t, and derived dynamical quantities (E, L_Z). After FoF-topology checking and boundary resolution, the final catalogue contains 1,180 Stellar Snake candidates with 4,196 base nodes and 692,408 unique member-star entries. Derived parameters are compared with external open-cluster catalogues and spectroscopic benchmarks. We introduce a graph-relation Snake Reliability Index (SRI) with Gold/Silver/Bronze grades to quantify structural coherence. A spatial-kinematic partition diagnostic identifies candidate subdivisions and provides core scores. At the population level, the catalogue shows an age--metallicity pattern in the jointly inferred parameters, a declining upper envelope of observed member-star entries toward older inferred ages, and a projected association between young Snake nodes, nearby spiral-arm loci, and the Radcliffe Wave. This homogeneous inventory provides an observational foundation for probing the formation, coherence, and dynamical evolution of hierarchical stellar complexes in the Milky Way.
